origin.rerun: python3 scripts/ci/check_soak_contracts.py --base origin/main  # after committing a pipeline update of an open check_observation item with no observation block; and grep -n 'due_by' scripts/ops/pipeline.py (is_due)

terminal_reason: Both halves fixed in PR #16973 (merged 2026-10-08): (1) check_soak_contracts no longer treats an UPDATE record of an item that was already check_observation at base as a new definition-of-done question (_prior_next_action); (2) the tooling gap is closed by `pipeline.py --redate ID --observation TEXT --next-due DATE`, which sets cadence, due_date and observation.due_by TOGETHER. Self-tested.
what: TRAP for any session updating pipeline records: (1) scripts/ci/check_soak_contracts.py fails guards on ANY newly added record for an open next_action=check_observation item that has neither due_when.soak, a SOAKS.json contract, nor an `observation: {what, how_to_check, due_by}` block -- an UPDATE record counts as 'new', so a plain re-date of 249 such items fails CI; (2) pipeline.is_due() treats observation.due_by as due REGARDLESS of check_every_days/last_checked, so changing cadence alone does not move an item that carries a due_by (190 open items did). BACKLOG-BURNDOWN-3 hit both: guards red on #16539/#16540, and its first schedule ignored due_by. Fix landed in-lane by setting cadence, due_date and observation.due_by together; the tooling gap is that pipeline.py has no 'redate' helper that does so.
